extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary mathematics instructors / college math faculty / mathematics educators
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for designing and implementing equitable, alternative assessment and grading systems in college-level mathematics courses, including exams, standards-based grading, specifications grading (EMRN), ungrading, and peer-feedback (PAR) workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable exam practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions for making exam use more equitable, including avoiding timed exams when possible and offering alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timed exams put pressure and invoke stereotype threat. Alternatives include take-home exams (less time pressure), allowing resource use (notes, etc.) to reduce pressure, group exams to build interdependence, and offering exam corrections. These strategies reduce time pressure and create access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards-based grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on measuring student progress on a set of well-defined learning objectives, often implemented via rubrics that show progress along several dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards-based grading requires students to demonstrate particular standards across topics and allows continued improvement during the semester, lowering the stakes of any individual assessment. Instructors must decide which assignments/problems contribute to standards and the extent to which revisions or repeated attempts are allowed; ideally unlimited attempts, but practical limits often apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifications grading (EMRN rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a simple, common rubric for most assessments; example EMRN rubric with four categories: E (Excellent/Exemplary), M (Meets Expectations), R (Revision Needed), N (Not Assessable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMRN definitions: E = work exceeds expectations and could be a model; M = mostly correct and reasonably communicated but improvable; R = partial understanding with significant gaps; N = too much missing to assess. Communicate expectations via rubrics or exemplars; allow revisions (treating revisions as new assessments for workload reasons); combine specification-based assignments into bundles to compute final grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMRN simplified M/R option
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplify EMRN to a binary meets/needs revision scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMRN can be reduced to M/R (meets expectations or revision needed) for quicker pass/fail grading while retaining opportunities for revision; helps manage instructor workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ungrading / collaborative grade determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Students and instructor collaborate to determine final grades, using student reflection and evidence rather than instructor-imposed scores alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices include students writing multiple reflective memos describing progress, co-constructing explicit learning criteria or rubrics, students using course assessments as evidence, and a final conversation where the student proposes their grade and discusses evidence. This shifts power dynamics and supports student agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoupling grades and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid combining grades with written feedback because grades reduce the value of feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide many opportunities for assessment and feedback that are not tied to grades (low-stakes). Use grades selectively and separate from formative feedback to preserve the pedagogical value of comments and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment as a tool for learning (formative philosophy)
rubrics_metrics.description: View assessments as part of the learning cycle and as tools to produce learning, not only as post-hoc measures for assigning grades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize collective progress and collaborative tasks, low-stakes practice testing, and formative tasks that elicit understanding (procedural and conceptual). Recognize limits of quantifying all learning and focus on opportunities that promote growth and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions for implementing alternative grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical implementation choices for alternative grading systems: what to grade, which assignments count, revision policies, and how final scores are computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no single correct implementation — methods can be combined (e.g., standards-based rubrics plus specifications grading). Limit the number of assessments if allowing revisions (treat revisions as new assessments), create bundles of learning targets to compute course grades, and build in flexibility and room for growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting participation data (use EQUIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather local, quantitative data about classroom participation to identify hierarchies and inequities rather than relying on gut impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulate student contributions, annotate maps of participation, or use formal tools like EQUIP (free customizable web app) to generate visualizations and analyze quality/distribution of participation. Recording teaching (with student notice) and/or having observers/student assistants collect data are recommended methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused peer observation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Use peer observations with specific, concrete goals rather than vague questions about overall teaching quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a clear objective for observation (e.g., 'Which students raise their hands when asked?'; 'How am I using student thinking?'). Use formal protocols like EQUIP to structure observations and feedback for targeted improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAR problem-solving feedback checklist (communication & heuristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: In PAR packets for problem solving, provide checkboxes/icons for strengths and items to request feedback on; suggested communication/heuristic checklist items include: show all steps, explain why not just what, avoid pronouns, use correct definitions, define variables/units, create diagrams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students reflect (check/circle icons) about what they did well and what they want feedback on; peer feedback uses these categories to provide concrete suggestions. The checklist supports clarity and higher-quality mathematical communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAR problem-solving accuracy checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist items focused on mathematical accuracy: correct setup, accurate calculations, solve multiple ways, answer reasonable/units, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside communication checklist to ensure both procedural correctness and conceptual robustness; peers and instructors can mark strengths and suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAR proof packet annotation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: A structured workflow for proofs where students draft a solution (left column), annotate (right column), receive peer annotations, revise, and submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stages: Draft (at home), Annotate (in class peer review), Revise (at home), Submit (in class). Annotation column is used to explain responses to peer feedback, and peer/self labels are used on annotations to track sources of feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-constructed grade-level descriptors (example A–F rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe characteristics of A/B/C/D/F students collaboratively (example from a syllabus): behaviors and quality of work associated with each letter grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example descriptors: A = attend, put forth work/effort, participate/helpful, complete assignments/quizzes on time, revise when necessary, strong reflections, demonstrate mastery; B = participates majority of time, completes most assignments, understanding mostly at mastery but presentation weaker; C = inconsistent, superficial understanding; D/F = lower levels of work. Use all course assessments as evidence during final student-instructor grade conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating expectations with exemplars and rubrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Make expectations explicit via rubrics or exemplars that describe high-quality work and different levels of understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For specification or standards-based grading, accompany rubric categories with exemplars to show concrete models of E/M/R/N levels. Clear communication of expectations is essential for these systems to work effectively.
